subject: SCIENCE
title: Plant Parts and Jobs
objective: Identify common plant parts and functions while recognizing variation.
introduction: Milo checks a plant: roots take in water, a stem carries it, and leaves use light to make food. Which part does each job?

vocabulary.definition: A living thing that grows in soil and makes food.
The part of a plant that holds it in the soil.
The part of a plant that carries water up.

items.prompt: Maxine examines roots, a stem, leaves, and flowers in a garden. Which statement is true?

options.text: Many flowering plants have roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds, but parts vary by plant and stage.
Roots use mouths to drink water

items.explanation: Plants can have different parts at different stages. Roots, stems, and leaves have jobs, while soil supplies support and nutrients rather than being plant food.

items.prompt: Milo gently lifts a plant and sees roots in the soil. Which pair matches a plant part to its job?

options.text: Leaves hold the plant in the soil
Flowers carry water to every leaf

items.explanation: Roots take in water and hold the plant in place. Leaves use light to make food, and stems help support and transport water.

items.prompt: Milo reads four plant cards. Which statement is NOT true?

options.text: Leaves use light to make food

items.explanation: Plants make their own food in leaves using light. Soil can provide water and nutrients, but it is not food that the plant eats.

items.prompt: A small plant stays upright because a part grows into the soil. Which part often anchors it?
items.explanation: Roots grow into soil and hold the plant in place. Flowers and fruits have other jobs and do not anchor the whole plant.

items.prompt: Maxine looks at a green leaf in sunlight. Which plant part-and-job pair is correct?

options.text: Flowers soak up water from soil
Leaves often use light to make food

items.explanation: Leaves use light to make sugars for the plant. Roots take in water and stems transport it, while flowers can help make seeds.
